organism.common_description: Ediacaran self-similar glide-reflected rangeomorph frond (Mistaken Point and Charnwood Forest)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_locus: apical primordium of a rangeomorph frond, where the smallest-order element spacing is selected before proximal expansion

paleobiology.note: No earlier named Charnia chronospecies is in this series, and the rangeomorph frond has no Cambrian successor past the boundary near 538.8 Ma. Charnwood Bed B is cited near 560 Ma by later authors; Mistaken Point, the other Avalonian Charnia surface, is the 565 Ma datum used by this chronoseries.

scale_delta_vs_organ_sibling.what_changes: At 140.4 µm the selected quantity is the apical chemical wavelength k_c. At 6.322 mm the same frond expresses expanded primary branches. The wavenumber ratio is 6322 µm / 140.4 µm = 45.03, so a shared reaction time would require the detail-scale diffusivity to be about 45^2 times smaller. Kinetics (a, b, D_u, D_v) are chosen for this apical regime and are not read from the sibling stub.

equations.activator: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + D_u laplacian(u)
equations.inhibitor: dv/dt = b - u^2 v + D_v laplacian(v)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = larger eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
equations.glide: phase(right) = phase(left) + pi, inherited from the midline onto the expanded frond

empirical_claims: Ford 1958 named Charnia masoni from a frondose fossil in Charnwood Forest.
Antcliffe and Brasier 2007 and Brasier, Antcliffe and Liu 2012: the frond is organized by glide reflection, not by the bilateral symmetry of a sea pen.
Narbonne 2004 and Hoyal Cuthill and Conway Morris 2014: rangeomorphs are modular and fractally branched.
Dunn, Liu and Donoghue 2018 and Dunn et al. 2021: growth is apical, with proximal differentiation, and Charnia is interpreted as a stem-eumetazoan.
The 140.4 µm wavelength is the assigned detail-tier scale of this loop. It is not a pigment-stripe measurement reported in those papers.

reported_in_source: Glide-reflected rangeomorph architecture, apical growth, and a Late Ediacaran age.
Turing 1952 dispersion relation and Schnakenberg 1979 kinetics, as published mathematical models, not as Ediacaran biochemistry.
reconstructed_in_script: Schnakenberg parameters (a, b, D_u, D_v) = (0.14, 0.93, 0.062, 1.35) scaled so lambda_c = 0.0001404 m.
Equal-diffusion negative control, same-phase ablation versus half-period glide, chevron-angle embedding fit to one cast.
transfer_boundary: The cohort form-class words 'pigment stripe' and 'ocellus' name the Turing pattern family. Charnia preserves relief branching, not a demonstrated ocular pigment.

A museum cast at centimetre scale is compared with a render whose chemical wavelength is 140 µm. Only shape statistics (outline, orientation, glide offset) cross that scale gap; the photograph does not resolve 140 µm.
does_not_claim: Does not claim Ediacaran tissues ran this Schnakenberg reaction.
Does not claim 140.4 µm was measured on the holotype.
Does not claim a Cambrian descendant or a pre-565 Ma Charnia chronospecies.
